title: Marketplace onboarding flow UX: subscription confirmation → org linking → entitlement validation + error states
creator: Chris Osei
content:
## Context
Marketplace buyers (AWS + GCP) are hitting friction between “Subscribed” and “First successful API call”. Current drop-offs are concentrated in:
- entitlement propagation delays (subscription not yet visible to Redwood)
- confusion around linking to an existing Redwood org vs creating a new org
- unclear next steps after provisioning (where to get an API key / endpoint / quickstart)

This ticket defines the console UX for the marketplace-specific onboarding entrypoint and the required error/edge states.

Primary user types:
1) Procurement-led enterprise buyer: expects marketplace purchase → immediate entitlement + clear account linking.
2) PLG buyer using marketplace for billing: expects self-serve flow, minimal waiting, retry guidance.

## Goals
- Reduce time-to-first-success (subscription → first successful request)
- Make entitlement state obvious and actionable (retry vs wait vs contact support)
- Prevent accidental org fragmentation (duplicate org creation when an org already exists)
- Handle edge cases gracefully (existing orgs, multiple subscriptions, region/residency constraints)

Non-goals:
- Redesign of general (non-marketplace) onboarding
- Pricing/plan selection UI (handled in marketplace listing / SKUs)

## Entry points
### A) Marketplace → Console deep link
User comes from AWS/GCP marketplace “Set up your account” / “Configure” CTA.
- Required query params (proposed):
  - provider=aws|gcp
  - marketplaceAccountId (or provider account identifier)
  - productCode/skuId (provider-specific)
  - optional: region

### B) Console → “I purchased via a marketplace”
Secondary entrypoint in standard onboarding (for users who close the marketplace tab and later return).

## Proposed flow (happy path)
### Step 0: Marketplace welcome + what happens next
Screen: “Connect your marketplace purchase”
- Shows provider badge (AWS / GCP)
- Short checklist:
  1) Verify subscription entitlement
  2) Link to an existing Redwood org or create a new org
  3) Provision access + generate an API key
- Primary CTA: “Verify entitlement”
- Secondary CTA: “I don’t see my subscription” (opens troubleshooting modal)

### Step 1: Entitlement verification (loading)
State: spinner + “Checking your marketplace entitlement…”
- Microcopy: “This can take a few minutes after purchase.”
- Auto-poll behavior proposal:
  - poll every 10s for up to 2 minutes
  - then stop and show “Still waiting” state with explicit retry

### Step 2: Link or create org
If user is already authenticated:
- If user belongs to 1 org: default select that org, show “Continue”
- If multiple orgs: require selection
- If no org: prompt to create

If user is not authenticated:
- Auth gate with SSO-aware language:
  - “Sign in to link your subscription”
  - if SSO domain detected, offer “Continue with SSO”

Copy requirements:
- Avoid implying that AWS/GCP account == Redwood org
- Clarify that org is the billing + access boundary in Redwood

### Step 3: Provisioning
Screen: “Setting up your org”
- Displays progress steps:
  - Entitlement validated
  - Org linked
  - Limits/quotas applied
  - (optional) Dedicated/Private provisioning initiated
- Expected time messaging:
  - Hosted: usually < 1 minute
  - Dedicated/Private: “We’ll contact you to finalize capacity/networking” (hand-off path)

### Step 4: First key + first request
Screen: “You’re ready to make your first call”
- Primary CTA: “Create API key” (if no key exists)
- If key exists: “Use existing key” + option to create a new one
- Provide:
  - API base URL
  - example curl
  - link to marketplace quickstart docs
- Secondary CTA: “Invite teammates”

## Required error states
### E1) Entitlement not found (most common)
Trigger: entitlement verification returns NOT_FOUND
Screen title: “We can’t find your subscription yet”
Body:
- Explain propagation delays and account mismatch as top causes
- Provide actions:
  1) “Retry entitlement check” (primary)
  2) “Confirm you subscribed with the right account” (expands guidance)
  3) “Contact support” (pre-filled with provider + marketplaceAccountId + timestamp)

Guardrails:
- Do not display raw account IDs by default; show last 4 or masked.
- Avoid language that sounds like we received their data if not validated.

### E2) Entitlement pending / delayed propagation
Trigger: provider indicates pending/processing OR Redwood sync job hasn’t ingested
Screen title: “Your subscription is still syncing”
- Show: “Typical: 5–15 minutes”
- Buttons:
  - “Check again”
  - “Notify me by email” (optional, if we support)
  - “Contact support”

### E3) Subscription already linked to a different org
Trigger: entitlement is valid but already associated with orgId != selected org
Screen title: “This subscription is already connected”
- Show org name (if user has permission) OR “another org” if not.
- Actions:
  - “Switch org” (if user has access)
  - “Request access to the org” (support workflow)
  - “Contact support”

### E4) User lacks permissions to link subscription
Trigger: user is not org admin / billing admin
Screen title: “You don’t have permission to link this subscription”
- Actions:
  - “Ask an admin to complete setup” (copyable instructions)
  - “Switch org”
  - “Contact support”

### E5) SKU/region mismatch or residency constraint
Trigger: marketplace purchase is for region/offer not supported by the user’s target deployment
Screen title: “This purchase can’t be activated in the selected region”
- Provide:
  - which region was detected (masked where needed)
  - supported regions link
  - CTA to switch region (if applicable)
  - contact sales/SE for Private/VPC needs

### E6) Multi-subscription conflict
Trigger: multiple active marketplace subscriptions detected for same provider account and org
Screen title: “Multiple subscriptions detected”
- Explain:
  - we can associate multiple subscriptions to one org, but need a primary billing source per product surface
- Provide selection UI:
  - list subscriptions by nickname + start date + SKU name
  - allow “Set as primary”

## UX / content requirements
- Keep buyer-friendly wording; avoid internal terms (“metering dimension”, “productCode”) in UI.
- Provide consistent support routing:
  - Enterprise: “Contact your Solutions Engineer” (when we detect Dedicated/Private SKUs)
  - Self-serve: “Contact support” + docs links
- Ensure accessibility:
  - all state changes announced (ARIA live region)
  - loading states not color-only

## Analytics / instrumentation notes (for ENG-22114)
Events we need to support (names illustrative):
- marketplace_onboarding_entrypoint_viewed
- marketplace_entitlement_check_started / succeeded / failed (error_code)
- marketplace_org_link_started / succeeded / failed
- marketplace_provisioning_started / completed
- marketplace_api_key_create_clicked / succeeded
- marketplace_first_request_help_clicked (if we provide guided first-call)

## Deliverables
- Figma file (wireframes + final comps + redlines): https://figma.com/file/REDACTED/DES-912-marketplace-onboarding
- Copy deck / strings for implementation (attached in Figma as “Dev strings” section)
- State diagram export for docs + eng handoff

## Design decisions (locked)
1) Polling entitlement check is time-boxed; after 2 minutes we switch to explicit retry to avoid “infinite spinner”.
2) Org selection is required when user has multiple orgs; we won’t auto-pick silently.
3) Error states include a single clear primary action + a secondary “Contact support” with prefilled context.

## Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should we expose marketplace account ID in UI?
  - A: No; only masked form + include full ID in support payload.
- Q: Can non-admin users complete setup?
  - A: No; show permission error + admin instructions.

## Handoff checklist
- [x] Final comps approved by PM (Nikhil Sharma) and Console owner (Chloe Martin)
- [x] Error codes aligned with ENG-22110 entitlement verification API
- [x] Support entrypoints validated with Dev Patel (support escalation)
- [x] Security wording reviewed by Marcus Lin (avoid over-claiming; no data-handling promises in UI)
